summary:
ASTRA (Astronaut Situational Tracking & Risk Assessment) is an AI-assisted astronaut health monitoring and risk assessment platform designed to support crew health during long-duration space missions.

The platform integrates multiple health-monitoring modules covering physical health, cognitive and behavioural indicators, radiation exposure, and physical deterioration associated with altered gravity. Its risk engine analyses health indicators against individual baselines and longitudinal trends to identify potential anomalies and emerging health concerns. An AI-assisted insights module translates these observations into understandable, actionable information for mission support teams.

ASTRA aims to address the challenges of maintaining astronaut health in environments where continuous medical supervision and conventional healthcare facilities are limited. By bringing multiple health indicators into a unified monitoring interface, it seeks to support earlier risk identification, informed decision-making, and improved crew health management during future exploration missions.
details:
ASTRA is designed as a unified astronaut health-monitoring and risk-assessment platform for future long-duration space missions.

The application is organised into six interconnected modules:

  1. BioMonitor – consolidates physiological indicators and tracks deviations from individual health baselines.
  2. NeuroTrack – monitors behavioural indicators, sleep patterns, cognitive performance, stress and fatigue.
  3. RadiationWatch – presents radiation exposure information and associated risk indicators.
  4. Bone & Fitness – tracks physical fitness indicators and potential musculoskeletal deterioration associated with microgravity.
  5. Risk Engine – analyses multiple indicators, historical trends and deviations to identify potential emerging concerns.
  6. Mission Health AI – provides AI-assisted explanations, summaries and suggested areas requiring attention.

The platform uses a unified mission dashboard to make complex health information easier to interpret. Its intended benefit is to support crew-health awareness, early identification of concerning trends and informed mission-support decisions.

The prototype uses simulated astronaut telemetry and demonstration datasets where actual mission measurements are unavailable. It is intended as a research and decision-support prototype, not a clinically validated diagnostic system.

The development process combines interface prototyping, software development, data visualisation and AI-assisted analysis. Its creative aspect is the integration of physical, behavioural and environmental health indicators into one mission-oriented system.
